message.content:
Below are the most common ways to terminate **Visual Studio Code** (`code.exe`) from a Windows command prompt (or PowerShell) using `taskkill`.  
Feel free to copy‑paste the command that best matches your situation.

---

## 1. Kill *all* VS Code instances (forceful)

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – match the image name.  
* `/F` – force the process to terminate (no graceful shutdown).

---

## 2. Kill *all* VS Code instances **and their child processes**

VS Code spawns several helper processes (`code.exe`, `code -insiders.exe`, `node.exe`, etc.).  
To make sure everything goes away:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

* `/T` – also terminate child processes that were started by the matched process.

---

## 3. Kill a *specific* VS Code instance by PID

First find the PID:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

Then kill that PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <PID> /F
```

Replace `<PID>` with the number you saw in the list.

---

## 4. Kill only your own VS Code processes

If you’re on a multi‑user machine and want to avoid touching other users’ VS Code:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq %USERNAME%"
```

---

## 5. Kill only *running* VS Code processes

Sometimes you want to ignore those that are already stopped:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "STATUS eq RUNNING"
```

---

## 6. Quick PowerShell alternative

If you’re in PowerShell, you can do the same thing with a single line:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

---

### Quick recap

| Scenario | Command |
|----------|---------|
| All VS Code instances | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` |
| All VS Code + children | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` |
| Specific PID | `taskkill /PID <PID> /F` |
| Only your own | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq %USERNAME%"` |
| Only running | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "STATUS eq RUNNING"` |

---

#### A note on “graceful” shutdown

`/F` forces the process to exit immediately.  
If you want VS Code to close cleanly (save work, run shutdown hooks), omit `/F`:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe
```

But be aware that if the process is hung, it may not terminate.

---

**That’s it!**  
Just run the command that fits your needs, and VS Code will be gone.
